title: Rigveda 1.106: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.106: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.106 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 74v-75r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.106.1-5 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 7, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 74v
translation.original_text:
1indra̍m mi̱traṁ varu̍ṇam a̱gnim ū̱taye̱ māru̍ta̱ṁ śardho̱ adi̍tiṁ havāmahe | ratha̱ṁ na du̱rgād va̍savaḥ sudānavo̱ viśva̍smān no̱ aṁha̍so̱ niṣ pi̍partana ||
2ta ā̍dityā̱ ā ga̍tā sa̱rvatā̍taye bhū̱ta de̍vā vṛtra̱tūrye̍ṣu śa̱mbhuva̍ḥ | ratha̱ṁ na du̱rgād va̍savaḥ sudānavo̱ viśva̍smān no̱ aṁha̍so̱ niṣ pi̍partana ||
3ava̍ntu naḥ pi̱tara̍ḥ supravāca̱nā u̱ta de̱vī de̱vapu̍tre ṛtā̱vṛdhā̍ | ratha̱ṁ na du̱rgād va̍savaḥ sudānavo̱ viśva̍smān no̱ aṁha̍so̱ niṣ pi̍partana ||
4narā̱śaṁsa̍ṁ vā̱jina̍ṁ vā̱jaya̍nn i̱ha kṣa̱yadvī̍ram pū̱ṣaṇa̍ṁ su̱mnair ī̍mahe | ratha̱ṁ na du̱rgād va̍savaḥ sudānavo̱ viśva̍smān no̱ aṁha̍so̱ niṣ pi̍partana ||
5bṛha̍spate̱ sada̱m in na̍ḥ su̱gaṁ kṛ̍dhi̱ śaṁ yor yat te̱ manu̍rhita̱ṁ tad ī̍mahe | ratha̱ṁ na du̱rgād va̍savaḥ sudānavo̱ viśva̍smān no̱ aṁha̍so̱ niṣ pi̍partana ||
translation.text:
1CALL we for aid on Indra, Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni and the Marut host and Aditi. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
2Come ye Âdityas for our full prosperity, in conquests of the foe, ye Gods, bring joy to us. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
3May the most glorious Fathers aid us, and the two Goddesses, Mothers of the Gods, who strengthen Law. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
4To mighty Narâṣansa, strengthening his might, to Pûshan, ruler over men, we pray with hymns. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
5Br̥ihaspati, make us evermore an easy path: we crave what boon thou hast for men in rest and stir. Like as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 74v (OPenn image 76, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.105.16 ‹yaḥ panthāḥ ādityaḥ divi›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 75r, begins in RV 1.106.6 ‹kutsaḥ vṛtra-hanam śacī-patim kāṭe›. Verses 1.106.1-5 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.106.6-7 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 7, varga 24); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 75r
translation.original_text:
6indra̱ṁ kutso̍ vṛtra̱haṇa̱ṁ śacī̱pati̍ṁ kā̱ṭe nibā̍ḻha̱ ṛṣi̍r ahvad ū̱taye̍ | ratha̱ṁ na du̱rgād va̍savaḥ sudānavo̱ viśva̍smān no̱ aṁha̍so̱ niṣ pi̍partana ||
7de̱vair no̍ de̱vy adi̍ti̱r ni pā̍tu de̱vas trā̱tā trā̍yatā̱m apra̍yucchan | tan no̍ mi̱tro varu̍ṇo māmahantā̱m adi̍ti̱ḥ sindhu̍ḥ pṛthi̱vī u̱ta dyauḥ ||
translation.text:
6Sunk in the pit the R̥ishi Kutsa called, to aid, Indra the Vr̥itra-slayer, Lord of power and might. Even as a chariot from a difficult ravine, bountiful Vasus, rescue us from all distress.
7May Aditi the Goddess guard us with the Gods: may the protecting God keep us with ceaseless care. This prayer of ours may Varuṇa grant, and Mitra, and Aditi and Sindhu, Earth and Heaven.
